points.confidence: Provisional label agreement for timing is reported in Study 04; lexical counts are deterministic.

points.title: Give the camera, the subject and the world their own sentences
points.finding: Detailed video prompts describe what the camera does, what the subject does and what the environment does in separate statements, rather than one blended description.
points.frequency: Provisional components in the mean film's video texts: camera motion {{t04a}}, action {{t04b}}. Lexical camera wording: {{t04c}} of the mean film's video prompts (pooled {{t04d}}).
points.evidence_note: Case wording is observed; component shares are inferred from provisional labels.
points.strength: moderate: separation is shown in cases; shares only show presence
points.study04: Study 06 subject, camera, environment, events, audio and invariants in named spans: confirmed, without a dedicated environment-motion label.

example.excerpt: tracking with her, handheld tremor ... Roopa hauls right to left ... Heavy rain falls in every frame.

points.denominator: Sampled successful video texts in {{p01h}} films; {{p04h}} nonempty video prompts in {{p01h}} films
points.competing_explanation: Presence of both components does not show they were separated; separation may be a writing habit with no effect on output.
points.confidence: Provisional labels; lexical counts deterministic.

points.title: Say what each reference is allowed to decide
points.finding: Some creators state the scope of a reference's authority, for example that one image governs the whole shot, instead of leaving the model to weigh several inputs.
points.frequency: Panel films with a creator-declared reference authority: {{t05a}} of {{t02f}}.
points.evidence_note: The creator's own instruction about a reference; whether the model obeys is not observed.
points.strength: weak to moderate: purposive panel only
points.study04: Study 03 property location in prose or metadata with unknown media: confirmed.

example.excerpt: This single reference image is authoritative for the entire shot.

points.denominator: {{t02f}} panel films
points.competing_explanation: Authority wording may be boilerplate; panel selection is purposive; no population census of authority wording exists.
points.confidence: Single-coder panel coding; {{t05b}} of {{t02f}} panel films could not be coded.

points.title: Put exclusions inside the main prompt
points.finding: The separate negative-prompt field is almost unused; creators write what they do not want, such as music, voices or subtitles, into the main prompt instead.
points.frequency: Nonempty negative-prompt fields: {{t06a}} in {{t06b}} films. Exclusion wording in the mean film's prompts: video {{t06c}}, image {{t06d}}. Provisional exclusion component in video texts: {{t06e}}.
points.evidence_note: Field states and lexical counts; the component share is inferred from provisional labels.
points.strength: strong for field use; exclusion wording is broad
points.study04: Study 06 lexical exclusion proxy: changed. It gains a provisional sampled semantic measure.

example.excerpt: "camera":"locked frame on the dial and hands" ... no voice, no music

points.denominator: Negative-role fields in all {{l01a}} films; {{p04h}} nonempty video and {{p04i}} nonempty image prompts
points.competing_explanation: The negative field may be hidden in the interface for most models; exclusion keywords include common words in other senses.
points.confidence: Deterministic field and lexical counts; provisional semantic share.

points.title: Continue from the previous clip
points.finding: To carry action across clips, creators feed an earlier video back in, either guiding a new clip from it or declaring an extension, and say where to pick up.
points.frequency: Films with video guided by an earlier video: {{t07a}} of {{p01h}} video-bearing films. Declared extensions: {{t07b}} jobs in {{t07c}} films.
points.evidence_note: Recorded video inputs and declared extension mode.
points.strength: strong for the routes; continuity achieved is not observed
points.study04: Study 07 raw input reuse or branch: undecided.

example.excerpt: frame 1 same last frame from here <<<video_1>>>

points.denominator: {{p01d}} video jobs in {{p01h}} films
points.competing_explanation: Video inputs may be used for style or motion transfer rather than continuation; extension availability depends on the model.
points.confidence: Deterministic route counts; the media are not inspected.

points.title: Combine source images and give each one a job
points.finding: Composite image requests attach several images and say what to take from each, sometimes as an ordered checklist of properties to match.

points.study04: Study 05 integration properties and sheet, plate or poster purpose in cases: confirmed.

points.title: Short edits ride on an attached image
points.finding: Very short edit requests are almost always attached to an image and rarely use camera language; the image carries the context and the text names only the change.

points.finding: About a third of prompts use section labels, such as foreground, middle ground and background, to organise a description. Machine-style JSON prompts are rare.

points.title: Revise a clip by naming the fix and keeping the rest
points.finding: Video revisions bound to an earlier clip ask for a specific fix and say everything else stays; video edit wording comes with preservation wording more often than other video prompts do.

points.title: Whether any technique works
points.finding: Every technique above is an instruction or a binding, not an outcome: no output was watched or judged. Testing them needs Study 12's controlled experiments, for example a reference sheet against a text description of identity, staged against one-pass generation, a local edit against regeneration, and continuing from a last frame against re-referencing.

points.evidence_note: The follow-up experiments are proposals.
